name: UKH Uptime Monitor
author: khamami

sections.description:
UKH Uptime Monitor monitors your WordPress site 24/7 and sends you an email alert the moment your site goes down.

Features

  • Automatic Monitoring — Checks your site every 5 minutes via WP-Cron
  • Email Alerts — Get notified instantly when your site goes down or comes back up
  • Uptime Dashboard — See your uptime stats at a glance (24h, 7d, 30d)
  • Response Time Tracking — Monitor your site’s response time
  • Public Status Page — Share a status page with your visitors using [ukhug_status]
  • Dashboard Widget — Quick status check from your WP dashboard
  • Activity Log — Complete history of all checks (kept for 90 days)
  • Lightweight — No external dependencies, no bloat

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. UKH Uptime Monitor starts checking your site every 5 minutes
  3. If your site goes down, you receive an email alert immediately
  4. When your site comes back up, you receive a recovery notification

Shortcode

Use [ukhug_status] on any page to display a public status page.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the ukh-uptime-monitor folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install via the WordPress plugin screen
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Go to UKH Uptime Monitor in the admin menu to configure settings
  4. Set your alert email and click “Check Now” to test
sections.faq:
How often does it check my site?

Every 5 minutes (300 seconds) via WP-Cron.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The plugin uses WP-Cron which runs in the background. The check itself is a single HTTP request that takes less than 1 second.

Can I change the check interval?

The free version checks every 5 minutes. Custom intervals are available in the Pro version.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. UKH Uptime Monitor makes HTTP requests like a regular visitor, so it works with all caching plugins.

What happens if my site is down?

You’ll receive an email alert with details about when the outage started and what error was detected. When the site comes back up, you’ll receive a recovery notification.

Can I share a status page with my visitors?

Yes! Use the shortcode [ukhug_status] on any page to display a public status page.

Does it store data locally?

Yes. All data is stored in your WordPress database. No data is sent to external servers.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Fixed: Author/Plugin URI now point to a working URL (www.ukhtechnologies.my.id).
  • Removed: “Tested up to” from main PHP file header (readme is the only source).
  • Fixed: Public status page attribution now requires explicit opt-in (default off).
  • Updated: Contributors list.

1.0.2

  • Fixed: Public status page no longer displays attribution by default (Guideline 10 compliance).
  • Added: Optional “Powered by UKH Uptime Monitor” credit toggle in settings (opt-in).
  • Fixed: Contributors list now includes the WordPress.org username.

1.0.1

  • Renamed to a distinctive, brand-prefixed name (UKH Uptime Monitor).
  • All functions/classes/options now use the ukhug_ prefix (4+ chars) to avoid collisions.
  • Fixed security: HTTPS verification (sslverify=true) now enforced on monitoring requests.
  • Fixed settings form to use the WordPress Settings API (options.php) so configuration is saved.
  • Prefixed custom cron schedule (ukhug_five_minutes) to avoid collisions.
  • Updated Plugin URI to working subdomain wp.ukhtechnologies.my.id.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Automatic uptime monitoring every 5 minutes
  • Email alerts for downtime and recovery
  • Uptime dashboard with 24h/7d/30d stats
  • Response time tracking
  • Public status page via shortcode
  • Dashboard widget
  • 90-day activity log
